subject: Elysian Labs - surge/burst clauses & autoscale ops for Dedicated
messages:
From: Ravi Kumar <ravi.kumar@elysian.ai>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, priya@elysian.ai
Cc: procurement@elysian.ai
Date: Tue, 12 May 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: surge windows & contract language questions

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Elysian is excited about the Dedicated offering. Before procurement signs off we have two items that need to be nailed down so we can finalize the SOW and the purchase order:

1) Burst / surge behavior: our traffic has predictable spikes during nightly ingest and an occasional product demo day where usage jumps 10-12x for ~3 hours. We need to confirm how burst capacity is guaranteed (reserved shoulder vs transient spot pools), how long redeploys take, and what eviction/backfill behavior we should expect.

2) Autoscale policy and billing: procurement wants a clear definition in the contract for when burst is billed at committed vs overage rates, and whether there are minimum-instance protections for model-serving kernels to avoid cold-start latency.

I've attached the draft SOW and a capacity snapshot from last month (capacity_matrix_elysian.xlsx) to give you a sense of the spike profile. Ideally we can map the SOW language to specific autoscale knobs so our operations team can exercise them during a staging test.

Can you loop in whoever owns Dedicated ops and a technical owner who can speak to GPU packing and preemption behavior? Procurement is hoping to get the final doc this week.

Thanks,
Ravi Kumar
Head of Platform Engineering
Elysian Labs

Attachments: capacity_matrix_elysian.xlsx, Elysian_DRAFT_SOW_v3.pdf

From: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Ravi Kumar <ravi.kumar@elysian.ai>, Priya Shah <priya@elysian.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: surge windows & contract language questions

Ravi — thanks for the context and the files. High level answer up front: we can meet the 10-12x short-lived spikes without changing the committed slab if we configure a shoulder buffer + transient burst pool and a short cooldown policy; billing can be modeled as committed units + transient usage billed at the agreed burst rate with a 30-minute metering window.

Quick proposal (summary):
- Baseline committed: 120 A100-equivalent GPU units (works with your steady-state ML traffic).
- Shoulder buffer: 20% of committed (adds ~24 GPUs) kept warm; used for <6 hour continuous spikes without eviction.
- Transient burst pool: up to 200 ephemeral GPUs (spot-backed) available for short spikes; preemption tolerance required for non-critical workloads.
- Metering: 30-minute intervals for burst billing; first 10 minutes of a sudden spike are not billed at burst rate if shoulder buffer covers it (i.e., crediting to reduce noise from short blips).
- Minimum-instance protection: reserve 8 GPU-backed replicas for hot model kernels per customer to prevent cold-start cascades during rapid scale-downs.

I'll attach a capacity matrix with these numbers and a short redline we typically include in SOWs for burst billing mechanics. Marcus will follow up with technical constraints (packing, preemption, eviction thresholds). Monica will add the monitoring/runbook pieces we recommend for production readiness.

Proposed next step: I can produce a short contract paragraph that maps the above to SOW line items — would you prefer that as a tracked Word redline or a DocuSign-ready clause? Procurement: what is your preferred format?

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Lead, Dedicated
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Elysian_DRAFT_SOW_v3.pdf (annotated), capacity_matrix_elysian_v2.xlsx

From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Ravi Kumar <ravi.kumar@elysian.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: surge windows & contract language questions

Ravi / Naomi — tagging in a few technical details so the SOW text is actionable for your ops team. I kept it short; happy to expand into an appendix.

Technical notes (for SOW appendix):
- GPU equivalence and packing: our "A100-equivalent" is a billing abstraction. On the infra side we pack by tensor memory footprint and kernel compatibility; heavy KV cache workloads can require dedicated slots. We'll reserve the 8 hot replicas as Naomi suggested; they map to pinned CUDA contexts to avoid warm-up.
- Transient burst pool behavior: ephemeral nodes are spot-preemptible. Eviction policy: when preempted we have a 60s drain hook to flush KV cache; long-running streams will be signaled for failover to committed lane if possible.
- Cooldown + scale-down policy: avoid scale-to-zero on model-serving tasks; enforce a minimum 10-minute cooldown with linear scale-down to avoid cascaded cold starts.
- Throttling failover: if burst pool is exhausted we fall back to a smaller, cheaper hosted model variant (latency trade-off documented) rather than dropping requests. This is configurable per-route.
- Ops hooks & SLIs: expose per-route token latency p95, burst-utilization, preemption-rate, and warm-replica-count. We can wire these into your PagerDuty with runbook links.

Operational impacts for Elysian: if you expect repeated >6 hour spikes we should convert part of the transient pool into short-term committed slabs to avoid sustained preemption exposure.

--Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Ravi Kumar <ravi.kumar@elysian.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: surge windows & contract language questions

Ravi / team — adding the monitoring and runbook items we recommend to avoid surprises during your demo days. Short checklist: 

- Pre-demo dry-run: run staged traffic at 12x baseline for 2x duration of expected demo to validate shoulder & burst behavior.
- Alerting: Burst-utilization > 70% for 15m -> notify ops and auto-escalate to Redwood on-call.
- Failover test: monthly test that simulates spot-preemptions and verifies fallback to hosted-variant within 90s.
- Cost burn dashboard: show committed vs burst spend per 30m window; procurement wants visibility into burst spend trends.
- Contact list: provide a 24/7 escalation contact for the first 90 days after go-live.

I've drafted a one-page runbook and a Playbook link for your team. I can attach the runbook as a PDF if you'd like.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Dedicated
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Elysian_Dedicated_Runbook_v1.pdf

From: Ravi Kumar <ravi.kumar@elysian.ai>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@elysian.ai>, procurement@elysian.ai
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: surge windows & contract language questions

Thanks Naomi, Marcus, Monica — that all looks good and aligns with what the execs want to see. A couple of quick asks from procurement and legal: 

- Please add the following to the SOW redline: a clause that defines "burst hours" (we propose: any contiguous >30-minute window where burst usage exceeds 25% of committed for more than 30 minutes) and caps daily burst chargeable hours at 10 hours unless pre-approved.
- We need the DocuSign-ready contract by EOD Wednesday (19 May) so procurement can route signatures before month-end.

I've attached our preliminary redline (Elysian_Contract_Redline.docx). We prefer the final clause in Word tracked changes. Also please confirm whether the 30-minute metering window you mentioned is aligned with billing systems (not all clouds support sub-hour metering for GPU).

If you can provide a DocuSign link once you have the final redline I'll route it immediately.

Appreciate the fast follow-up.
Ravi
Head of Platform Engineering
Elysian Labs

Attachments: Elysian_Contract_Redline.docx
